summary: Idempotency tenant-scoping fix (1) verified correct: TenantGuard is a global APP_GUARD running before interceptors in Nest lifecycle, every route using @UseInterceptors(IdempotencyInterceptor) requires auth (no @Public route uses it) so req.tenant is populated by the time the interceptor runs; the 'no-tenant' fallback stays safe because userId remains part of the cache key; the new cross-tenant regression test genuinely exercises req.tenant?.['id'] (would fail on a req.tenant.tenantId-style typo). Marketing-publishing atomic claim (3) verified correct: IS DISTINCT FROM correctly treats NULL as distinct from 'published', so a first-time publish (publication_status NULL) is not rejected by the new atomic claim WHERE clause; concurrent claim race is properly closed via affected-count check. ai-jobs fail-closed guard (4) verified: placed before any DB-touching code, does not short-circuit valid jobs. However, notifications dedup fix (2) has a real gap: handleSend() does a SELECT-then-INSERT check for job.id in metadata with no unique constraint/index and no locking, so a BullMQ stalled-job redelivery reassigned to a second worker while the first is still finishing (a real at-least-once scenario) can pass the existence check on both workers concurrently, producing a duplicate row and duplicate WS push -- the exact race class the sibling marketing-publishing fix in the same wave correctly closed with an atomic UPDATE...WHERE. Filed as find-32bf2e0a.
